conventions.convention: Φ(a+bi)=(a,b); real-linearity uses the canonical embedded real scalars and does not mean complex-linearity.

Complex paths are continuous maps on nonempty closed intervals [a,b], a≤b. Length is the extended-real supremum of polygonal sums; singleton length is separately defined as zero without invoking a partition.

Piecewise-C1 means interior differentiability on each closed piece with a continuous derivative extension to that piece; adjacent derivative extensions need not agree, and zero-speed pieces are permitted.
Reparametrizations are continuous, surjective, and weakly monotone in either direction; pauses are allowed, and a singleton target has no nontrivial orientation.

load_bearing.statement: The coordinate bijection Φ(a+bi)=(a,b) is a bijective isometry and a homeomorphism; it preserves all real affine combinations and transports openness, closedness, boundedness, compactness, connectedness, interior, closure, and boundary in both directions.

For a continuous complex path on [a,b] with a<b, length is the extended-real supremum of finite sums of chord moduli; rectifiability means these sums have a real upper bound. Singleton paths have length zero and are rectifiable.

Every continuous complex path has the same polygonal sums and length as its coordinate path, including singleton intervals; it is rectifiable exactly when both coordinates have bounded variation. Under the stated finite piecewise-C1 hypothesis, length is the sum of the Euclidean speed integrals.
For all z,w∈C and r∈R, Φ(z+w)=Φ(z)+Φ(w) and Φ(rz)=rΦ(z).
For open U⊆C, z∈U, and f:U→C, the coordinate map f_R is totally differentiable at Φ(z) exactly when some real-linear L has remainder |f(z+h)-f(z)-L(h)|/|h| tending to zero; then Df_R(Φ(z))=Φ∘L∘Φ⁻¹.
For a continuous complex path γ:[a,b]→C and a continuous surjective nondecreasing or nonincreasing map φ:[c,d]→[a,b], L_C(γ∘φ)=L_C(γ), including infinite lengths and singleton intervals.
